As a Jewish name borne by several rulers in Judea, it is a reminder of the complexity of Jewish history and culture. Herod the Great, specifically, is known for ordering the massacre of the innocent children in Bethlehem in an attempt to kill the newly born King of the Jews, Jesus Christ. This event serves as a poignant reminder of the potential darkness that can lurk in power and authority. Similarly, the name Herod can be seen as a call to maintain a balance between worldly power and spiritual thriving, and to never let worldly ambitions cloud one's true purpose and calling as a follower of Christ.
